MlxForeignABI.Rule: extern("sysv") follows the x86_64 System V ABI, including its aggregate classification.
extern("win64") follows the Windows x64 ABI, including 32-byte shadow space and its aggregate rules.
extern("syscall") is target-defined raw syscall ABI; on Linux x86_64 syscall number is rax and arg4 uses r10 instead of rcx.

extern("c"), and extern without an ABI string, declares a bodiless foreign function with the target's C ABI (System V on x86_64, AAPCS64 on aarch64). It is imported from a shared library at load time under its source name; no library is named in source, the dynamic linker searches the output's needed libraries.
An export fn is visible to the dynamic linker under its source name and follows the target's C ABI, so foreign code can call it.
Integer arguments and results narrower than 64 bits crossing a C ABI boundary are sign- or zero-extended by the receiving side, since AAPCS64 leaves their upper bits unspecified.

A program with foreign or exported functions is written as a dynamically linked executable (PT_INTERP /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, DT_NEEDED libc.so.6 plus each --library NAME, immediate binding through R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT GOT slots). Calls through function pointers are treated as possibly foreign: AL carries the vector-register count for variadic callees on direct foreign calls, and narrow integer results are extended after every foreign or indirect call and narrow parameters on entry to every function (System V leaves bits above 32 unspecified). An exported function may run on a thread C created: it saves the caller's r14/r15 and reloads the aggregate arena registers from the data words _start recorded. A linked program exits through the C library's exit so stdio is flushed and library destructors run.
MlxForeignABI.CABITypes: c_char c_schar c_uchar c_short c_ushort c_int c_uint c_long c_ulong c_longlong c_ulonglong c_float c_double c_size c_ssize
MlxForeignABI.NoRequiredCParser: Compiler conformance does not require a C preprocessor, C parser, Clang, libclang, or header translator.
